samples.summary: The PDF export's new stylesheet wait + 5s timeout race has no test at all
samples.evidence: `exportSlidesPdfAndDownload` gained the load-bearing behaviour this PR exists for: it now awaits `Promise.race([Promise.all(families.map(ensureFontLink)), setTimeout(FONT_CSS_TIMEOUT_MS)])` BEFORE `document.fonts.load`, and the header comment calls the stylesheet wait "THE LOAD-BEARING HALF" (glyph-subset previews would otherwise be what the deck rasterises with). Nothing tests it: no assertion that `document.fonts.load` is only called after the link promises settle, none that a never-settling stylesheet falls through after ~5s rather than hanging the download, and none that a family whose link errors still lets the export proceed. Searched `packages/frontend/tests` for `exportSlidesPdfAndDownload`, `pdf-actions`, `collectFontFamilies`, `FONT_CSS_TIMEOUT`, `document.fonts.load` — zero matches; `tests/app/slides/**` has no export test and the only `pdf-*` tests are the PDF viewer/comment ones under `tests/app/files/`. Regressing the ordering (dropping the await) would leave every suite green.

samples.summary: "a second call for the same family awaits the first request" cannot fail — it never checks that the second promise is still pending
samples.evidence: The test calls `ensureFontLink(FAKE_A)` twice, asserts one link exists, dispatches `load`, then `await Promise.all([first, second])`. Every assertion holds whether the second call returns the shared `fullLinkSettled` promise or an already-resolved `Promise.resolve()`. The latter is exactly the failure mode that matters here: a caller (the PDF export, above) that awaits the second call would proceed before the `@font-face` rules parsed and rasterise the preview subset — the bug this PR was written to fix. The `fullLinkSettled` WeakMap is new behaviour and this is the only test naming it, so it is fake coverage. A real check would assert `second` is unresolved before the `load` event (e.g. race it against a microtask/timer sentinel).

samples.summary: "selecting a previewed-only family still loads the full family" supplies the behaviour under test as its own `onChange`
samples.evidence: The test renders `FontFamilyPicker` with `onChange: ensureFontLink`, so the full-load it then asserts on is performed by the callback the TEST passed in, not by any production wiring. In `src`, the picker never calls `ensureFontLink` on selection (font-family-picker.tsx:181 just calls `onChange`); production callers wire `ensureFontLink`/`ensureFont` only to `onPrefetch` (hover) — e.g. slides/toolbar/text-edit-section.tsx:68 — and `app/slides/theme-builder-panel.tsx:172,179` pass no `onPrefetch` at all. So the framed regression ("a family the user only ever scrolled past must still load in full when they pick it") is asserted about a test-local wiring; the library-level dedupe it exercises is already covered by ensure-font-link.test.ts:145. No test covers a real pick path promoting a subset to a full load.

samples.summary: The `fullSettled` failure branch (recent rows must still become previewable when the full-catalog load fails) is untested
samples.evidence: The new `.finally(() => setFullSettled(true))` and `previewable = entry !== undefined || fullSettled` exist specifically so a FAILED full-library load still unblocks recent rows at default weights. The only test that touches this (font-family-picker.test.ts:448) mocks `loadFullFontCatalog` to RESOLVE, so the reject path — the one where a permanently-unobserved row would silently never preview — has no coverage. Searched font-family-picker.test.ts for a rejecting mock (`Promise.reject`, `mockRejected`) and grepped the tests dir for `fullSettled`/`loadFullFontCatalog`: only the resolving stub at line 32.

samples.summary: The HMR fallback `fullLinkSettled.get(existing) ?? Promise.resolve()` has no test
samples.evidence: A link present in the head with no WeakMap entry (module reloaded) must report settled rather than issue a second request. ensure-font-link.test.ts never constructs that state (it only ever creates links through `ensureFontLink` itself), so the `??` branch is unexercised — a change that instead returned a never-settling promise, or appended a duplicate link, would stay green. Searched ensure-font-link.test.ts and font-catalog.test.ts for a manually-injected `data-wafflebase-font` link: none.

samples.summary: The new shared build-if-stale helper (and its two re-implementations in design-sandbox) is untested
samples.evidence: `buildDesignEditorIfStale` encodes the exact rule the PR narrative says cost hours twice — stale when EITHER artefact is missing or older than the newest of `src/**` + `vite.shell.config.ts` + `tsconfig.build.json`. Nothing asserts it: the two consumers boot dev servers so they never run in CI, and `verify-scenes.mjs`/`verify-tokens.mjs` each carry a hand-copied duplicate of the same predicate (the very divergence the extraction was meant to end) with no test tying them to the shared one. Searched scripts/test/*.test.mjs and packages/design-editor for any spec naming `build-if-stale`/`buildDesignEditorIfStale` — only the callers. The new verify-self-lanes assertions cover the LANE graph, not this predicate.

finding.evidence: `exportSlidesPdfAndDownload` gained the load-bearing behaviour this PR exists for: it now awaits `Promise.race([Promise.all(families.map(ensureFontLink)), setTimeout(FONT_CSS_TIMEOUT_MS)])` BEFORE `document.fonts.load`, and the header comment calls the stylesheet wait "THE LOAD-BEARING HALF" (glyph-subset previews would otherwise be what the deck rasterises with). Nothing tests it: no assertion that `document.fonts.load` is only called after the link promises settle, none that a never-settling stylesheet falls through after ~5s rather than hanging the download, and none that a family whose link errors still lets the export proceed. Searched `packages/frontend/tests` for `exportSlidesPdfAndDownload`, `pdf-actions`, `collectFontFamilies`, `FONT_CSS_TIMEOUT`, `document.fonts.load` — zero matches; `tests/app/slides/**` has no export test and the only `pdf-*` tests are the PDF viewer/comment ones under `tests/app/files/`. verdict.reason: The claimed behaviour is real: packages/frontend/src/app/slides/pdf-actions.ts:38-59 awaits Promise.race([Promise.all(families.map(ensureFontLink)), setTimeout(FONT_CSS_TIMEOUT_MS=5_000)]) before the document.fonts.load loop, with the header comment (lines 24-30) calling the stylesheet wait the load-bearing half. No test reaches it. Repo-wide grep for exportSlidesPdfAndDownload yields only the definition, slides-export-button.tsx:21/99, and markdown docs; repo-wide grep for imports of `pdf-actions` yields only docs-export-button.tsx:18 and slides-export-button.tsx:21 (no test), so it isn't reached indirectly either. I also checked places the reviewer did not: colocated src tests (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/*.test.* = insert-image, theme-fonts, toolbar/arrange-menu, toolbar/index), the slides package export tests (packages/slides/test/export/pdf.test.ts:177-197, pdf-chart.test.ts:138-151 — these test collectFontFamilies/exportSlidesPdf inside the slides package, never the frontend wait), the visual browser harness (packages/frontend/scripts/verify-visual-browser.mjs:390-493 — a screenshot font-settle gate for index.html's floor fonts, not the export), harness.config.json:69-79 (bundle budget only), and packages/docs/test/export/pdf-fonts.test.ts (server-side docs font cache). The nearest existing coverage, packages/frontend/tests/components/text-formatting/ensure-font-link.test.ts:169-200, asserts only that ensureFontLink's own promise settles on load/error — it does not assert that document.fonts.load runs after the links settle, that a never-settling stylesheet falls through after ~5s, or that an erroring link still lets the export proceed. Dropping the await in pdf-actions.ts would leave every suite green, so this is a behaviour change with no meaningful test (major under the test-adequacy rubric).

Every assertion holds whether the second call returns the shared `fullLinkSettled` promise or an already-resolved `Promise.resolve()`. The latter is exactly the failure mode that matters here: a caller (the PDF export, above) that awaits the second call would proceed before the `@font-face` rules parsed and rasterise the preview subset — the bug this PR was written to fix. verdict.reason: The test exists exactly as described and is vacuous for the behavior it names. ensure-font-link.test.ts:194-200 calls ensureFontLink(FAKE_A) twice, asserts only that one <link> exists, dispatches 'load', and awaits Promise.all([first, second]) with no assertion at all about `second` still being pending. The behavior under test is font-catalog.ts:182 (`if (existing) return fullLinkSettled.get(existing) ?? Promise.resolve();`) together with the new fullLinkSettled WeakMap at font-catalog.ts:138. Replacing line 182 with an unconditional `return Promise.resolve()` would leave every assertion in the test passing: link dedupe comes from the DOM lookup findFontLink (font-catalog.ts:122-131, 178), which is independent of the promise, and awaiting an already-resolved promise succeeds. So the test cannot fail for the shared-request semantics its title claims. The dedupe assertion it does make is already covered by 'is idempotent for the same family' (test line 63-67), and no other test covers the promise sharing (font-catalog.test.ts mentions ensureFontLink only in a comment at line 29). The failure mode is reachable and material: the module's own contract at font-catalog.ts:149-160 tells callers to await before document.fonts.load()/check(), and pdf-actions.ts is such a caller. Real, in-lane (fake coverage of a new behavior), and blocking under the test-adequacy rubric.
